title: The kubectl power kit: jsonpath, wait, explain, diff
summary: Ask precise questions with -o jsonpath and custom-columns, wait for real conditions, look up fields with explain, and review changes with diff before you apply.

steps.title: Precise questions, scriptable answers
body: kubectl get pods -A -o wide -L app -w                          # every namespace, wider, label column, watch
kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deploy/api --timeout=60s    # block until it is true (CI!)
kubectl explain deployment.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate            # field docs from the API server itself
kubectl diff -f k8s/                                               # what apply WOULD change (exit 1 if anything)
kubectl apply --server-side -f k8s/                               # merge on the server, track field owners
`jsonpath` and `custom-columns` read any field the API returns (`-o yaml` shows them all). `wait` replaces `sleep`
loops in scripts: it returns as soon as the condition holds, and fails at the timeout.

steps.prompt: Which command blocks until a Deployment has finished rolling out its pods and they are available?

steps.title: A one-line inventory, then wait for a rollout
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`). Deployments run in the namespaces `shop` and `payments`.
1. Write an inventory into `~/answers/deploys.txt`: one line per Deployment outside `kube-system`, as
`NAMESPACE/NAME REPLICAS IMAGE`, sorted. Use `-o jsonpath` (or `custom-columns`), not hand-typing.
2. `~/search.yaml` is a new Deployment whose pods take a few seconds to become ready. Apply it, then use
`kubectl wait` (not `sleep`) so that your command only returns once it is **Available**.

checks.name: deploys.txt is the inventory
checks.cmd: diff <(kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \(.spec.replicas) \(.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)"' | sort | grep -v '^kube-system/' | grep -v '^shop/search ') <(sed '/^$/d' ~/answers/deploys.txt | grep -v '^shop/search ' | tr -s ' ')
checks.fail: Not the inventory. `kubectl get deploy -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name} {.spec.replicas} {.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -v ^kube-system | sort`.

checks.name: search is Available
checks.fail: `search` is not Available with 2 ready pods yet. `kubectl apply -f ~/search.yaml`, then `kubectl wait -n shop --for=condition=Available deploy/search --timeout=60s`.

hints: `-A` lists every namespace; `{range .items[*]}...{"\n"}{end}` prints one line per item.
The image is at `.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image`; drop `kube-system` with `grep -v` and `sort` the rest.
solution: kubectl get deploy -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name} {.spec.replicas} {.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -v '^kube-system/' | sort > ~/answers/deploys.txt
steps.explain: `jsonpath` makes kubectl answer exactly the question you have, in a shape a script can use, across namespaces. `kubectl wait` is the honest version of `sleep 30`: it returns the moment the condition holds and fails loudly if it never does, which is what CI pipelines and runbooks need. Note that `Available` waited for the readiness probe, not just for the containers to start.

steps.prompt: Before applying a teammate's change to `k8s/` in production, what shows you exactly what would change in the cluster?
steps.explain: `diff` asks the API server to compute the result of the apply (with defaults, webhooks and other owners' fields) and shows it as a diff; it exits 1 when there is a difference, so CI can use it for drift checks. `--dry-run=client` only renders locally and knows nothing about the live object.

steps.prompt: Look up what `maxSurge` accepts without leaving the terminal.
steps.explain: `kubectl explain` reads the API server's own schema (CRDs included), so it is always right for the cluster and version you are on. `--recursive` prints the whole tree under a field.
